exposure: Maternal vitamin D depletion (low vitamin D diet)
cohort: The participants were preterm rat offspring born via cesarean section to female Sprague-Dawley rats assigned to either a low vitamin D or control diet.
finding: Maternal vitamin D depletion led to lower oxygenation and reduced survival time in preterm rat offspring, associated with reduced lung weight and birth weight at gestational day 19.
followup_time: Up to 1.25 hours after birth (survival time)
